basis: We chose these values and they may not be ideal; the report re-ranks the languages under random perturbations of all of them and only calls an order stable if it survives. Cell score = reach x route factor x product of the factors of its `needs` (the obstacle factors in weights.json). Integration score = weighted mean of I1-I5 (Absent counts 0). Combined = exposure x w_exposure + integration x w_integration.

routes.why: The language's own compiler or standard toolchain does it, nothing added to the build recipe.
One or more extra tools from the language's own project or the Bytecode Alliance: installed, versioned and invoked by the developer, but supported and documented.
Extra tools from a third party (a package, a plugin, a fork): works, but the language project does not stand behind it.
The developer writes the glue (string marshalling over alloc/analyse): no tool, every project repeats it, errors show up at run time.

I1.name: WASI
I1.question: Can the module run outside a browser, as a command-line program?
I1.test: A program copies stdin to stdout; run under `wasmtime run`. Text and empty input must round-trip.
I1.counts: The route (built in, library, hand-written imports) and the WASI version (p1, p2, p3).

I2.name: Component Model
I2.question: Can the language compile to a WebAssembly component with a typed interface?
I2.test: A `words` component exports a WIT function taking a string and returning a record; its type is checked against the reference WIT and it is called with `wasmtime --invoke`.
I2.counts: Only direct support: a toolchain or generator for the language. A hand-written canonical ABI is not support.

I3.name: JS bindings
I3.question: Can a string and a record cross to JavaScript without hand-written marshalling?
I3.test: The same `words` function is called from Node with a string and returns an object, through whatever glue the language's tooling generates.
I3.counts: The route: built in, official tool, community tool, or hand-written glue.

I4.name: Debuggability
I4.question: Does a debug build carry what a debugger needs?
I4.test: A debug build of `life`: name section, DWARF or a source map, and a trap whose stack names the source function.
I4.counts: Full if names plus DWARF or a source map are present; partial if only names.

I5.name: Size
I5.question: How much does the language add to a small module?
I5.test: `life`, `words` and `cat`, each built as a size-tuned floor build and a default-flags build, measured after `wasm-opt -Oz`.
I5.counts: Bytes on a log scale: 1000 times the smallest build of a program scores 0.
